Hi Jordan / Priya —

Great to be moving this forward. Attached is a first-pass MAP focused specifically on the technical gating items we discussed during the demo: org & service account setup, API key issuance, IP allowlist, and the VPC peering window. Key ask: we want to align on a two-week activation runway we can mutually commit to so HealthLytics can start running production-like load tests by week 3.

Summary (high level) — please review and confirm:
- Week 0 (today): Agree MAP & sign-off (owner: HealthLytics legal + Redwood sales).
- Day 1–2: Provide org admin email and list of dev/test accounts that need access.
- Day 3–5: Redwood issues environment API keys (ephemeral keys for POC) and uploads initial allowlist; customer provides IP ranges.
- Day 6–8: VPC peering window (coordined maintenance) — networking team to exchange routes and complete peering.
- Day 9–14: Canary tests, perf runs, and rollback checklist.

Open items for you:
1) Confirm which HealthLytics email will act as org admin for Redwood (we need an owner to finish org onboarding in our portal).
2) Share the firewall/IP ranges (CIDR) for the test VPC and any on-prem NAT IPs. I attached a small template to make this quick.
3) Do you need us to open a dedicated peering ticket with AWS/GCP or will your network team drive the cloud-side request?

Attachments: HL-MAP-draft-v1.pdf (MAP draft), network-allowlist-template.csv

If that runway looks good, Ben (cc'ed) will map this to specific timelines and call out the peering prerequisites. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps — suggested times Thurs/Fri.

Thanks,

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks for the quick responses. I'm Ben (solutions engineer) — I'll own the technical execution for the POC. Below is a concrete runbook that matches Vanessa's high-level MAP but with specific steps and acceptance criteria so your infra/security teams can sign off.

POC technical runbook (concise):
1) Org setup (Day 1)
   - HealthLytics provides org admin (priya.rao@healthlytics.io) and 1–2 dev/test accounts.
   - Redwood sends an org invite; admin accepts and confirms roles.
Acceptance: Admin is able to see the POC org in the Redwood console.

2) API key issuance (Day 3)
   - Redwood will create scoped, short-lived API keys for the POC (default TTL: 7 days).
   - We can provide a stricter rotation schedule on request (48h) — we support automated rotation via our keys API.
Acceptance: Test call to /v1/generate with sample prompt returns 200 and usage visible in console.

3) IP allowlist (Day 3–4)
   - We need your egress NAT IPs (CIDR or single IPs) to seed the allowlist. Use the attached network-allowlist-template.csv.
   - For peering verification we also accept internal RFC1918 ranges (x.x.x.0/24) if routing will be over peering.
Sample firewall entries we expect (example only):
   - 34.120.12.45/32 (egress NAT)
   - 10.20.30.0/24 (staging VPC range)
Acceptance: Redwood console shows the provided allowlist and API calls from those IPs are allowed.

4) VPC peering (Day 6–8)
   - Recommended process: HealthLytics initiates peering request in GCP (you create peering from staging VPC -> redwood-prod-peering).
   - Provide peering VLAN & project IDs and a contact OP for coordination (NOC email + phone).
   - Redwood will accept and route; route exchange limited to the staging prefixes only.
Acceptance: A ping/traceroute to the peer endpoint succeeds and our TCP healthcheck (443) returns 200.

5) Canary & perf (Day 9–14)
   - Run a 2-hour canary using representative queries (we'll provide a small workload script).
   - Capture median p50/p95 latency and token cost.
Acceptance: Canary succeeds with latency < 300ms p95 for the sample workload and errors < 0.1%.

Attachments: redwood-peering-checklist.xlsx (networking owners & steps), network-allowlist-template.csv

Notes & options:
- If you prefer not to peer, we can provide a whitelisted public endpoint with TLS mutual auth; that adds ~1 business day to setup.
- For keys rotation to 48h, we will schedule an automated rotation job and share the API token endpoint so you can integrate with your secrets manager.

Proposed confirmed dates based on your ask:
- Kickoff call: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:00 PT
- Peering window: Wed–Thu, 18–19 Nov 2026 (preferred, minimal traffic)
- Canary perf: Mon–Tue, 23–24 Nov 2026

If the dates work for you, Vanessa and I will schedule the kickoff and include Redwood networking + our NOC on the calendar.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0892
